title: Count inherited seam exposures and charge a deeper load-path reset
statement: If repair j leaves j seams in series during its service interval and every seam-interval independently survives with1-h, n repairs have survival(1-h)^[n(n+1)/2]. In a different model, partition n repairs into blocks m_j<=k, each starting with a new independent deep connection of failure probability s that fully unloads older seams. Then E=sum_j m_j(m_j+1)/2 and survival=(1-h)^E*(1-s)^q, q=ceil(n/k), including initial block establishment.

requires: Exact series-only load path and fixed independent seam-interval hazard0<=h<1; every inherited seam remains loaded in the stack model.
The reset alternative additionally acquires a deep host connection, complete old-seam unloading and fixed independent establishment hazard0<=s<1; n,k are positive integers,1<=k<=n.
provides: If repair j leaves j seams in series during its service interval and every seam-interval independently survives with1-h, n repairs have survival(1-h)^[n(n+1)/2]. In a different model, partition n repairs into blocks m_j<=k, each starting with a new independent deep connection of failure probability s that fully unloads older seams. Then E=sum_j m_j(m_j+1)/2 and survival=(1-h)^E*(1-s)^q, q=ceil(n/k), including initial block establishment.
assumptions: The two architectures have different physical controls and load graphs; initial graft success is not evidence of a durable bypass.
The square-root rule assumes0<h,s<1, many approximately equal blocks, a continuous k and no omitted costs; evaluate the finite discrete problem separately.
costs: Pay all inherited exposures, every block establishment, durable host-anchor inventory and actual reset work/material. No infinite renewal follows from fresh chemical sites alone.
contract.units: n,k,q,E count; h,s probabilities;a,c dimensionless log hazards. Host/used attachment inventories must use compatible units.
contract.obstruction: Measure the actual post-repair load graph and acquire renewable deep connections before using a favorable reset survival number.

body: The unreset stack counts1+...+n; chemical renewal does not remove those mechanical dependencies. A direct-host route may avoid old seams only by establishing a real load-bearing bypass. With nonrenewed host attachment inventory A_host and positive A_used per repair, number of such attachments is at most floor(A_host/A_used). For periodic blocks write a=-ln(1-h),c=-ln(1-s). When n is a large multiple of k and boundaries/discrete costs are neglected, negative log survival per repair=a*(k+1)/2+c/k; continuous minimization gives k≈sqrt(2*c/a), then integers/boundaries must be checked. This is not the exact finite-n optimum or a universal reset policy. The source code charges one establishment per block, including the first; a preexisting first support would have a different exponent. Correlation, aging, incomplete unloading or alternative load graphs change this contract.
